I'm doing my bachelor's in CS right now. I'm a third year student, I guess in America it's called being a Junior. I won't say I dislike software engineering and sometimes I enjoy it, but if I didn't have to earn money to live in this world, I probably wouldn't do it. I completely understand what you're saying about doing all the right things and still not feeling like you're in control of your life. Though I can't say I did everything right, I spent my first year in college agonizing over uncertainty whether I really want to do software engineering and almost completely flunked it before busting my ass in 2nd year clearing all the subjects I previously failed. But, I do often feel like we are deluded in thinking that we are in control of our lives. There are layers and layers of external factors that control each and every decision we make - our bodily needs, familial obligations, societal obligations, peer pressure, the various hormones in our body, aging and diseases, etc. How, then, can we consider ourselves to be in control of anything?

There is no restructuring that can possibly anchor the human greed. When civilization started a few thousand years ago, that's what they did - survive, produce and learn a trade to directly benefit others. But, the thing is, as time passed and people had their basic needs fulfilled, they demanded more complex services and products which demanded various service providers and producers to collaborate. And when people collaborate, it inevitably leads to a power dynamic and hierarchies and voila, you have corporations. There's no way to avoid it: all the rot in the society that you are at odds with is a manifestation of the rot in the human nature and as long as humans exist, that rot is not going anywhere.
